intro.buddy: Today we learn a superpower. It is called making ten.
intro.headline: Making ten
intro.body: When two numbers make 10 together, adding gets easy.
say: Today we learn a superpower. It is called making ten.
When two numbers make ten, adding gets easy.

teach.headline: Ten fills the basket
teach.body: Seven flower balls. Three crystal balls. Together they fill all ten spots. 7 + 3 = 10.
say: Seven flower balls, and three crystal balls.
Together they fill all ten spots.

teach.headline: Every number has a ten partner
teach.body: Eight needs two. Nine needs one. Seven needs three. Each number has one partner that finishes the ten.
say: Every number has a partner that makes ten.
Eight needs two. Nine needs one. Seven needs three.

teach.headline: Why it helps
teach.body: To add 9 + 4, make ten first. 9 + 1 = 10. Then add the 3 that are left over. That is 13.
say: To add nine plus four, make ten first.
Nine plus one is ten. Three are left over.
Ten and three more is thirteen.

guided.question: 9 needs how many to make 10?
guided.hint: Count up from nine. Nine, ten. That was one hop.
say: Nine needs how many more to make ten?

guided.hint: Six balls are in. Count the empty spots. Four!

reteach.headline: So close!
reteach.body: Making ten is tricky. Let's look at the trick one more time, then try the star check again.
say: Making ten is tricky. Let's see the trick again.

mastered.headline: You mastered Making ten!
say: You mastered making ten. Great work!
